Past analyses of AAPL (most recent first):

[2026-08-04 | AAPL | Hold | -1.4% | -1.3% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Hold

**Executive Summary**: Hold AAPL at benchmark/current weight — put no new common stock to work at 309.38, which sits mid-range between a three-times-tested 300.00–302.56 shelf and the falling 10EMA (320.45) / VWMA (323.70) supply stack. Deploy only on proof of absorption: a daily close above the 323.70–323.84 cluster on volume expanding beyond the ~75M post-shock run-rate, expressed with a defined-risk structure (e.g. a 324/333 call spread) rather than stock, sized so maximum loss is contractual at ≤0.5% of capital. Trim in two tiers — a modest cut on a daily close below 302.56 (08-03 low / lower Bollinger 302.03), a larger cut or collar on a close below 300.00, which opens 293–294 then the rising 200SMA at 278.54. Horizon 1–3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October Q4 print; because the 07-31 open gapped 8.6% through the prior close, treat any resting stop as indicative only.

**Investment Thesis**: All three risk seats converge on Hold, and unlike a manufactured consensus this one survives independent weighing: the strongest advocate will not buy at 309.38 (the aggressive analyst’s own entry is 324.00, 4.7% above spot) and the strongest skeptic will not sell the core ("I am not backing a sell" — the conservative analyst’s mandate is mechanics, not direction). That asymmetry is the finding, not the excuse.

Where the bear case is stronger and decides the day. The bear carried the only forward-looking argument, and the bull conceded its decisive point. Operating expenses grew 21.9% against revenue growth of 16.2% for the nine months, so 100% of the operating-margin expansion came from gross margin, which printed at a record/cyclical-high 50.06%. That makes the entire earnings trajectory levered to one line item, and the sensitivity is quantified in the material: roughly $4.9B pre-tax / ~$0.28 of EPS per 100bp. The two most probable causes of a 200–300bp reversal — memory/component cost inflation and tariff friction — are precisely the themes in the news flow (supply shortages; Apple testing Chinese memory suppliers). The bull’s answer was "I’ll manage the tripwire," which is not an answer for a quarterly reporter: by the time a sub-48% print arrives in late October, the repricing has already happened. Two further bear points went unrebutted. First, contract liabilities rose just 8.8% ($13.7B to $14.9B) against revenue +16.2% — a genuine deceleration in the Services bookings that the high-margin mix thesis depends on. Second, the "loading the spring" narrative rests on a $13.27B gross-intangible step-up that cannot be reconciled to the ~$3.56B residual investing outflow; both other analysts correctly insist that is a disclosure gap, not optionality, until the notes say so. The 12% buyback cut stripping ~2.4 points of per-share support is a real, if gradual, drag toward EPS/net-income convergence. And management’s own below-consensus guide, confirmed across two headlines, produced an idiosyncratic de-rating while the Dow made a record — a more negative signal than a beta-driven decline.

Where the bear overreaches. "Below the 50SMA" is 23 cents below a flattening line, not a trend break, with the 200SMA at 278.54 rising and 11.07% below spot. The 300.00–302.56 shelf has held on three separate tests (07-31 low 300.00, 08-03 low 302.56, 08-04 low 301.32, with the lower Bollinger at 302.03) while volume faded 132.49M → 75.05M → 68.00M, and the 08-04 session closed in the upper third of its range, +1.96%. The MACD line is still positive at 3.110 and the histogram decelerated to −0.54 from −1.61 — early deceleration, not a turn — and RSI recovered from 40.34 to 44.68. Most importantly, the conservative’s request to raise the trim to 302.56 amounts to selling the bottom of a nine-point range before the shelf actually fails, which is damage realization dressed as risk management. My own record bears directly on this: the 2026-07-22, 07-23, 07-24 and 07-27 AAPL de-risking calls each forfeited 3.2%–12.5% of alpha by cutting inside a still-rising structure without a printed trigger. The one pre-event Underweight that worked (07-28, −13.1% alpha) worked because a dated binary catalyst then hit — and that event has already hit and been absorbed once.

Where the aggressive case fails. The 324.00/309.50 add is not convex: the aggressive analyst’s own first objective, the 333.43 gap fill, pays 9.4 points against 14.5 points of stop risk (0.65:1), and only reaches 1.1:1 at the 340.08 record close. Worse, the 07-31 session opened 8.6% — roughly 28 points — through the prior close, so the "14.5-point defined risk" is indicative only and plausibly double that in a repeat. The stop also sits essentially at today’s close, meaning the trade risks a full round trip back to spot. The "fading volume = absorption" read is overstated: 68M shares is still above the ~55M prior 22-session average, i.e. fading panic, not exhausted supply. And converting an unreconciled $13.27B intangible build into "capital deployment optionality" is narrative, not analysis.

Why Hold rather than a directional call. The forward question is unresolved in both directions, and not merely because the analysts disagree — because the data to resolve it does not exist in this toolset. There are no valuation multiples of any kind (P/E, EV/EBITDA, FCF yield), no primary-source detail on the below-consensus Q4 guide, no Q4 consensus, no coverage of the 07-28–08-02 news window, and no options chain or IV. So the bull’s implicit "down ~9–10%, therefore cheap" is an assumption, and the bear’s "it can fall another 9% and still be expensive" is equally unproven. The business is not impaired (revenue +16.2% to $364.36B, gross profit and operating income both +21.7%, EPS +22.4% to $6.88, FCF +52.5% to $110.20B, net cash +$28.41B to $62.17B, debt down $14.31B, zero new long-term issuance in nine months) and the tape is not broken (rising 200SMA, shelf intact) — so Sell/Underweight is not supportable at the bottom of the range. But there is no edge at 309.38 and the margin cycle is unproven — so Buy/Overweight is not supportable either. Hold is the honest call.

What would change it. Upgrade toward Overweight on two consecutive daily closes above the 323.70–323.84 cluster with volume above the ~75M post-shock run-rate, scaling further only if a subsequent 10-Q shows gross margin holding at or above 49% and contract liability growth re-accelerating toward revenue growth (or on Q4 revenue re-acceleration that converts the $11.09B inventory / $7.645B raw-materials build from write-down risk into a ramp). Downgrade to Underweight on a daily close below 302.56 with the MACD histogram still negative and expanding, and toward Sell on a volume break of 300.00 that opens 293–294 and the 278.54 200SMA. Do not short outright into a rising 200SMA; if a hedge is required, use defined-risk options. Note explicitly that the 333.43 price target offered here is technical (gap-fill), not valuation-derived, because no multiple is available.

**Price Target**: 333.43

**Time Horizon**: 1-3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October Q4 FY2026 print

REFLECTION:
Five days produced -1.3% alpha (raw -1.4%), a mild negative drift against a Hold — but this window is far too short, and too shallow, to adjudicate a 1–3 month, late-October-catalyst thesis whose central claim was that 300.00–302.56 would hold. What it does undercut is the "no edge at 309.38" equilibrium: sitting at the midpoint of the range still cost relative performance while the shelf was never actually tested, so the Hold bought neither protection nor optionality. The lesson is to stop pricing a mid-range Hold as free — commit the trim/invalidation level in advance (a 302.56 close, not a feeling) and judge the decision against whether that level was touched, rather than crediting the shelf for a drift that never reached it.

[2026-08-03 | AAPL | Overweight | +1.7% | -0.3% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: Overweight AAPL — constructive, but staged, not committed at the $303.42 spot. Build 40–55% of a full standard weight over the next one to two quarters in three tranches, with tranche 1 capped at 3–4% of portfolio (not the 5–6% originally proposed, which risks 36–43 bps against a $288.7 stop, not the stated 25–30 bps). Tranche 1 fires only on a close above $311.8 on >100M shares, or two consecutive closes above $309.5 with the following session holding $309.5; the alternate half-size (~2%) flush entry is $294–$300 only on declining volume and a close off the lows, and nothing is bought if $302.3 breaks on volume. Tactical stop $288.7 on tranches 1–2, hard invalidation on a weekly close below the rising 200-SMA at $278.24, which flips the plan rather than trimming it. Target $340 with partial trims into $322.9–$325.1 and the $333.4 gap origin.

**Investment Thesis**: The business case is not in dispute and it is the reason this is not a Hold or a trim. The 2026-07-31 10-Q shows Q3 FY26 revenue of $109.42B (+16.4% YoY), gross margin 50.06% (+357 bps), operating margin 32.62%, diluted EPS $2.02 (+28.7%), 9M FCF of $110.20B (+52.5%), and net cash of ~$62.2B, up ~$28.4B in nine months. Receivables fell 21% on 16% revenue growth — the opposite of a channel-stuffing signature — and the conservative analyst himself conceded the franchise is intact. Against that, three successive prior AAPL Underweights (2026-07-21, 07-22, 07-23) each gave up +3.7% to +3.8% of alpha by trimming a fundamentally sound, structurally rising name on momentum decay alone. That history is the strongest argument against the conservative seat's conclusion here.

The conservative seat wins the entry and the sizing argument, and it wins with arithmetic rather than a narrative. Measured from the stated $311.0 trigger, upside to $344 is ~10.6% against ~7.2% to the $288.7 stop — roughly 1.5:1, not the "better than two-to-one" the aggressive analyst claimed by benchmarking from the $303 spot. A 5–6% tranche with a 7.2% stop risks 36–43 bps of portfolio, not 25–30 bps; the neutral analyst's 3–4% tranche (risking ~20–25 bps) is the correct expression of the plan's own risk budget. The tape also supports a higher bar: on 2026-08-03 AAPL opened $309.58, traded to $311.80 and was sold all day to a $303.42 close, within $0.86 of the session low, after the 07-31 gap from $333.43 to a $304.81 open on 132.5M shares (~2.6x normal). VWMA at $325.09 puts July buyers underwater as overhead supply, price sits 6% below the 10-EMA at $322.91 and pinned on the lower Bollinger band at $302.26, MACD histogram is -2.98 and deteriorating, and RSI 40.34 is not oversold. Unlike the 2026-06-25/26 reversal, which snapped back the next session on 261.8M shares and reached $308.63 by July 2, this bounce was sold. One close above the middle of a shelf that just rejected price is not confirmation.

The aggressive seat wins on structure and on the direction. Its central insight is that the plan is already a set of data gates — tranche 2 requires a higher low above $309.5 or a second consecutive hold of $294–$300, tranche 3 requires a close above the $322.9–$325.1 10-EMA/VWMA confluence — so "wait for confirmation" is already embedded. Its June precedent is real evidence that these repairs happen fast, which is why the conservative seat's full-repair bar (weekly close above $311.8 plus a two-session retest plus >100M shares plus a MACD cross) risks missing the entire first leg. The conservative also over-penalizes the reward/risk by pricing the tactical trade off the $278.24 structural kill, which is a plan-flip level, not the first tranche's stop.

The neutral seat's synthesis is the one that survives: keep the staged accumulation, make tranche 1 smaller (3–4%), tighten the trigger, cap the total target at 40–55% of full weight until the Q4 FY26 print resolves the supply and margin questions, and let the 60–70% target only be earned. The aggressive seat overreaches in dismissing supply and memory costs as a one-to-three-quarter air pocket when no Q4 FY26 revenue or gross-margin guidance figures are in the record and Cook's "evaluating all options" language explicitly extends cost pressure "beyond the September quarter." The conservative seat overreaches in implying no action: it concedes the franchise is fine and then sets a bar high enough to miss the move entirely.

What would change this: upgrade toward Buy on a volume-backed reclaim and hold of $311.8, or a close above $322.9–$325.1 with volume that proves July supply has been absorbed, or a Q4 FY26 print with gross margin near or above 48.5%, mid-teens revenue growth and intact guidance. Downgrade toward Hold/Underweight on Q4 FY26 gross margin below 48.5% (the bull's own line), finished-goods inventory building while revenue guidance decelerates, receivables or deferred revenue deteriorating against revenue, FY27 guidance revealing the ~$10B non-recurring cash-tax benefit did more of the work than assumed, an explanation of the $13.3B gross intangibles build implying acquisition spend with no visible return, or a weekly close below $278.24. Explicitly missing from the record and flagged rather than papered over: no consensus FY27 estimates, no reported Q4 FY26 revenue or gross-margin guidance figures, no footnote for the intangible build, no sentiment or insider data, and no knowledge of the caller's current holdings or cash — so sizing is expressed as a fraction of the caller's own standard AAPL weight, and the 48.5% gross-margin trigger is the bull's stated watch item, not reported guidance.

**Price Target**: 340.0

**Time Horizon**: Build over 1-2 quarters; thesis 6-12 months

REFLECTION:
The 5-day alpha of -0.3% against a +1.7% raw return is too short and too small to validate a staged 1–2 quarter accumulation plan — the window never tested the $311.8 trigger or the $302.3 invalidation, so the directional call remains unjudged rather than confirmed or refuted. What it does support is the thesis's anti-trimming core: AAPL rose modestly and lagged SPY only marginally, consistent with the argument that the prior three Underweights bled alpha by selling a structurally rising name on momentum alone, and it undercuts nothing in the $288.7/$278.24 risk architecture. The concrete lesson is to state explicitly at the outset that a gated, tranche-based plan cannot be scored over five days, so the review measures the gates hit and the alpha forgone by not being partially invested, not the P&L of a position the plan had not yet authorized.

[2026-07-31 | AAPL | Underweight | +1.4% | -2.1% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Underweight AAPL: trim roughly 30% of the existing position, targeting ~60–65% of standard weight, but execute into strength rather than into the 300 support that was just absorbed on the heaviest volume in the window. Stage it — a 10–15% tranche at/above the 308–309 area now, the balance working as a sell-limit at 312.66 with a two-session soft time stop, and if AAPL trades below 305 before the limit fills, take 10–15% at the prevailing price rather than pretending to get 308.91. Retained core: daily close below 300.00 cuts to 50–55% of standard, below 294.38 to 40–50%, and a break of the 200-SMA at 277.96 triggers a full thesis reassessment. Do not pre-authorize a 284–278 falling-knife buy. No leverage, size for ATR 9.87 (3.20% of price), horizon 1–3 months re-underwritten at the next print.

**Investment Thesis**: All three risk seats converge on the same direction — reduce AAPL — and disagree only on execution, which is the cleanest consensus in this record. What separates this from my five prior AAPL Underweights that lost money within five days (07-20 +3.2% raw, 07-21 +3.8%, 07-22 +3.8%, 07-23 +3.7%, and the 07-24 Hold at -7.2%) is that the trigger those lessons demanded has finally printed: a -7.35% close at 308.91 on 132.5M shares, ~2.6x the 50.8M average and the third-largest session in the data window, the first close below the 50-SMA (309.4994) since 06-30, the entire July leg round-tripped (07-02 breakout close 308.63), a MACD histogram flip to -1.3652, and price 5.35% below VWMA 326.39 and 5.60% below the 10-EMA 327.24 — a volume-weighted cohort now overhead. That is distribution on an earnings gap, not the sub-one-ATR momentum decay I incorrectly sold into four times in July.

The asymmetry is the second leg and the aggressive and conservative analysts agree on the arithmetic even while disagreeing on the label: ~+5.9% to the 324.37/326.39/327.24 confluence versus ~-10.0% to the rising 200-SMA at 277.96, with RSI 43.24 offering no oversold cushion (June's low was 32.20) and ATR at 9.87 having expanded from 8.06 two sessions earlier. Poor skew in both directions argues for shrinking, not for holding full size and hoping — which is why the neutral analyst's conclusion of "do nothing" is the weakest of the three positions.

The fundamental overlay caps the call at Underweight rather than Sell. The franchise is not broken: FQ3 revenue $109.4B +16.4%, gross margin 50.06%, operating margin 32.62%, diluted EPS +28.7%, nine-month FCF $110.2B, net cash $51.2B, and price still +11.14% above a rising 200-SMA.
